#!/bin/bash

# SQLite dump script
# Author: Red Canary
# Description: This script will dump the contents of the SQLite database to a file.

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f /tmp/gta.db ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database to a file
sqlite3 /tmp/gta.db.dump > /tmp/gta_dump.sql

# Print a success message
echo "Database dumped successfully."

SQLite Dump Script
=================
This script is used to dump the contents of a SQLite database.
It is a part of the Atomic Red Team, a collection of atomic-scale attacks and defense techniques.

Usage:
 ./sqlite_dump.sh <database_file>

Example:
 ./sqlite_dump.sh /path/to/database.db

Note:
  This script requires the sqlite3 command to be installed on the system.
  It also requires the database file to be in the same directory as the script.

# Atomic Test Name: T1005 - Timestomp
# Description: This atomic demonstrates the use of the timestomp tool to modify the timestamps of files on a system.
# Estimated time to complete: 10 minutes

# Download the timestomp tool

# Verify the timestamps have been modified
ls -l /path/to/file.txt

# Clean up
rm timestomp

#!/bin/bash

# SQLite Dump Script

# Check if the database file exists
if [! -f "gta.db" ]; then
  echo "Error: Database file 'gta.db' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Dump the database
sqlite3 gta.db.dump > gta_dump.sql

# Print the dump to the console
cat gta_dump.sql

# Remove the dump file
rm gta_dump.sql

#!/bin/bash

# SQLite dump script
# Author: @redcanaryco

# Usage: sqlite3 <database> <table> <output_file>

# Example: sqlite3 gta.db accounts accounts.txt

if [ $# -ne 3 ]; then
  echo "Usage: sqlite3 <database> <table> <output_file>"
  exit 1
fi

DB=$1
TABLE=$2
OUTPUT=$3

sqlite3 $DB "$TABLE".dump > $OUTPUT
